name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX)
objective: Study heptane and methanol droplets in O2/N2 mixtures diluted with a second inert gas (nitrogen, carbon dioxide, helium or xenon) to see how an inert suppressant changes the flammability limit of the two fuels.
what_varied: Ambient O2, inert diluent type and amount, pressure, droplet size.
flow_source: GUIDE p.33 (quiescent ambient); p.12 Fig. 2 (droplet translated at 3 cm/s)
sensors: analog color camera, radiometer, low-light-level UV camera, two HiBMs cameras (p.52)
key_result: The flammability limit is lower in reduced gravity; the limiting oxygen index (LOI) is significantly lower than in normal gravity and lower than predicted. Stable cool flames form after radiative extinction of heptane droplets.
implication: Terrestrial standards for inert-gas suppressants do not offer the same margin of safety in low gravity as in normal gravity.
source: NASA ISS Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC); PSI-69 (DOI 10.60555/mbq8-0451)

name: FLEX-2
fuels: mixtures of pure fuels, real-fuel surrogates; ethanol shown in Fig. 3
objective: Follow-on to FLEX: study fuel mixtures, real-fuel surrogates, soot formation, slow sub-buoyant convective flow and droplet-droplet interactions.
what_varied: Fuel type and mixture, diluent, convective flow, droplet spacing.
range_source: GUIDE p.12 (MDCA: 0-3 atm, up to 40% O2)
sensors: analog color camera, radiometer, low-light-level UV camera, two HiBMs cameras (p.52)
key_result: Fig. 3 shows sooting propensity differs between diluents for ethanol burning in 30% O2 at 2.4 atm.
source: NASA ISS Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC)

name: Laminar Soot Processes (LSP)
objective: Study soot processes in laminar gas-jet diffusion flames in a quiescent (ambient) configuration inside a sealed chamber.
source: NASA ISS Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC)

name: Turbulent Gas-jet Diffusion Flame (TGDF)
objective: Study a laminar gas-jet diffusion flame in which an iris at its base induced vortices in the entrained air (flame-vortex interaction).
what_varied: Vortex forcing by the iris mechanism.
source: NASA ISS Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC)

name: Enclosed Laminar Flames (ELF)
objective: Study flame stability of laminar gas-jet diffusion flames inside a fan-driven flow duct (crew operated in the Middeck Glovebox).
source: NASA ISS Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC)

name: Smoke Point In Coflow Experiment (SPICE)
objective: Study the transition from non-sooting to sooting coflow flames, aiming at simple predictions of soot emissions (smoke point).
what_varied: Fuel flow rate (Fig. 4: non-smoking to smoking tip as fuel flow increases).
sensors: digital still camera, video camera, air flow, fuel flow, radiometer (p.52)
key_result: Flames showed the transition from non-smoking to a fully open, smoking flame tip as fuel flow increased (Fig. 4).
source: NASA ISS Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC); Dotson et al., Fire Safety Journal 46 (2011) 550-555

name: Structure & Liftoff In Combustion Experiment (SLICE)
objective: Study lifting and lifted flames that detach from the burner and stabilize downstream, to improve combustion models for fuel efficiency and lower pollutant emission.
sensors: digital still camera, video camera, air flow, fuel flow, radiometer (p.52)
source: NASA ISS Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC)

name: Burning Rate Emulator (BRE)
fuels: gaseous fuels emulating paper, plastic, alcohol
objective: Improve understanding of materials flammability (ignition, extinction) and assess existing flammability test methods for low and partial gravity, using a porous burner whose gas flow mimics a burning solid or liquid.
what_varied: Gaseous fuel and flow rate (controlled from measured heat flux and surface temperature).
sensors: radiometers, two color cameras, low-light-level UV camera, two HiBMs cameras, photomultiplier tubes, ion current measurement, gas chromatograph (p.52)
implication: Focused on fire prevention in spacecraft; tests the relevance of flammability test methods for low- and partial-gravity environments.
source: NASA ISS Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC)

name: Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame (CLD Flame)
objective: Extend the range of flames that can be predicted (very dilute near-extinction and sooty flames) by developing and verifying kinetic and soot submodels.
what_varied: Fuel injection velocity and fuel dilution.
sensors: radiometers, two color cameras, low-light-level UV camera, two HiBMs cameras, photomultiplier tubes, ion current measurement, gas chromatograph (p.52)
source: NASA ISS Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC)

name: Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames (E-FIELD Flames)
objective: Understand flame-ion production and how ions can be used to control non-premixed flames.
what_varied: Electric field strength (up to 10 kV) and fuel dilution.
sensors: radiometers, two color cameras, low-light-level UV camera, two HiBMs cameras, photomultiplier tubes, ion current measurement, gas chromatograph (p.52)
source: NASA ISS Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC)

name: Flame Design (ACME)
fuels: ethylene (PSI-10 table); ethylene or methane planned
objective: Understand soot inception and control so that oxygen-enriched, robust, soot-free non-premixed flames can be designed; normal and inverse spherical flames.
what_varied: Injected fuel concentration and oxygen enrichment of the atmosphere; flow direction (normal vs inverse flame).
range_source: PSI-10 table (computed; 11 rows with XO2 'RAMP'/'LOW O2' excluded)
sensors: radiometers, two color cameras, low-light-level UV camera, two HiBMs cameras, photomultiplier tubes, ion current measurement, gas chromatograph (p.52)
source: NASA ISS Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC); PSI-10

name: Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames (s-Flame)
objective: Predict the structure and dynamics, including extinction, of soot-free and sooty spherical diffusion flames on a porous spherical burner.
what_varied: Fuel, inert diluents in fuel and chamber atmosphere.
sensors: radiometers, two color cameras, low-light-level UV camera, two HiBMs cameras, photomultiplier tubes, ion current measurement, gas chromatograph (p.52)
source: NASA ISS Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC)

name: Burning and Suppression of Solids (BASS)
fuels: flat samples, PMMA spheres, porous wax slabs, wax candles
objective: Examine burning and extinction of a wide variety of solid fuel samples in microgravity, to improve 1-g material fire-safety tests and guide extinguishing strategies.
what_varied: Airflow speed (main variable), oxygen (nitrogen dilution), nitrogen suppressant jet.
range_source: GUIDE p.19 (glovebox ISS air ~21% O2, one atmosphere; tests as low as 17% O2)
flow_source: GUIDE p.20 Fig. 11 (12 cm/s); Fig. 12 flow decreased from 10 to 'less than 1 cm/s' (lower bound not given as a number)
sensors: digital still camera, video camera, air flow, fuel flow, radiometer (p.52)
key_result: NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 is not conservative: materials can burn at lower oxygen in microgravity than on Earth. Local suppressant application was not adequate; the jet entrained air and sustained the flame, and nitrogen could even strengthen it.
implication: Materials screened as safe in 1-g may burn in a spacecraft; extinguisher placement needs rethinking because a suppressant jet can feed a microgravity flame.
source: NASA ISS Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC); PSI-26 (sample list only)

name: BASS-II
what_varied: Initial O2, fan/air flow settings (not cm/s), material and thickness (PSI-25 columns).
range_source: PSI-25 table (computed); no pressure column; flow is device settings, not cm/s
sensors: radiometer, camera frames, O2/CO2/CO gas analysis (PSI-25 columns)
source: PSI-25

name: Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction (SoFIE)
fuels: plastics such as PMMA or Delrin (likely candidates)
objective: Study and characterize ignition and flammability of solid spacecraft materials in practical geometries and realistic atmospheres (up to five investigations).
what_varied: Material, geometry, external heating, oxygen, pressure, flow speed.
sensors: same as ACME: radiometers, two color cameras, low-light-level UV camera, two HiBMs cameras, photomultiplier tubes, ion current measurement, gas chromatograph (p.52)
implication: Planned to test Space Exploration Atmospheres (reduced pressure, elevated oxygen) and evaluate oxygen margins of NASA-STD-6001 Test 1.
supp_source: GUIDE p.24 (ignition and suppression with external heat flux)
source: NASA ISS Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC)

name: Structure of Flame Balls at Low Lewis-number (SOFBALL)
objective: Test whether stationary spherical premixed flames (flame balls) can exist in very lean, low-Lewis-number mixtures.
key_result: Flame balls exist: the weakest flames ever burned (about 1 W), some lasting over 40 minutes until the experiment timed out.
source: NASA ISS Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC)

name: Water Mist Fire Suppression (Mist)
objective: Measure how water droplet diameter and water concentration affect the speed, strength and shape of premixed flames, to design better mist suppression systems replacing Halon.
what_varied: Water droplet diameter, water concentration, fuel and oxygen mixture.
key_result: Led to non-toxic water-mist portable fire extinguishers certified for spaceflight; the first two of nine reached the ISS in December 2015 to replace CO2 units.
implication: Direct path from microgravity research to a crew fire-suppression tool.
source: NASA ISS Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC)

name: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment (SAME)
objective: Measure the particle-size distribution of smoke from spacecraft materials.
key_result: Microgravity flames produce very different particulate sizes, so detectors that sense particulates need different signatures in space.
implication: Guidance for designers of future spacecraft smoke detectors.
source: NASA ISS Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC)

name: Candle Flames (Mir)
objective: Observe a candle flame in long-duration microgravity aboard Mir.
key_result: Microgravity candle flames burned over 45 minutes, to a lower ambient oxygen than an identical candle on Earth, and oscillated before extinction.
implication: Refutes the belief that a steady fire cannot exist in quiescent microgravity.
source: NASA ISS Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC); Dietrich et al. (2000)

name: Cool Flames (CIR initiative)
objective: Find the pre-conditions for hot-flame/cool-flame transitions, cool-flame stability and spontaneous re-ignition, using existing FLEX-2 MDCA hardware.
sensors: analog color camera, radiometer, low-light-level UV camera, two HiBMs cameras (p.52)
key_result: Builds on FLEX: after hot-flame extinction, heptane droplets kept burning with a low-temperature cool flame.
implication: Very weak, persistent flames invisible to the eye can spontaneously re-ignite long after the visible flame is gone.
source: NASA ISS Researcher's Guide: Combustion Science (NP-2015-10-034-JSC)
